title: 1690 / 2056 reference clone
family: Reference hybrid: floating pickup -> powered V banks -> stopped cradle
notice: Architecture clone; dimensions are provisional, not measured team CAD.
summary: 508 mm floating pickup and kicker feed a retained rear drive, two independent straightener banks, then a two-event stopped cradle. UNTESTED Stage-2 hybrid.
advantage: Independent side drives separate yaw control from pickup; retaining a rear powered contact and a stopped cradle targets low-momentum transfer and delayed handoff.
risk: Steep pickup, wheel preload, yaw and cradle sensor sequencing may stall or overrun; projected clearance is not a 3D or physical pass.
firstTest: Hand-crank a flat-plate fixture from rest at skewed entries; inspect every contact handover, full-coral bumper margin, two beams and absent-gripper hold.
inspiration: Reference chain, not a dimensional reconstruction: research/2025-coral/2056-binder.md records inspected binder PDF p.7: 20-inch acquisition, floating top roller, kicker and smooth ramp; p.9: opposing vertical-axis straightener banks with independent drives; p.11: stopped cradle, anti-bounce feature, gripper cutouts and two distinct beam events. Drawing OPR25-A11 versus A11-R1, PDF pp.7/8, supports the shared-to-independent drive change; A20-R1, p.22, supports split cradle and sensor mounting. P209, p.139, includes precision bends, so this proposal replaces those brackets with located flat plates and machined blocks. research/2025-coral/1690-1778.md E03, Korny's 1690 post 35, reports separating flexible acquisition from an internal orienter and restoring a rear roller after a static ceiling caused an installed dead spot. This is author-reported, not our test. Unlike 03's generic four-bar nose and single index-wheel pair, 11 explicitly follows this reference chain through seven wheels per independently driven side bank and a separately stopped, two-event cradle. 508 mm is the exact conversion of 2056's reported nominal 20-inch acquisition width, used here as mouth intent, not a measured clear opening. All other mechanism coordinates, wheel sizes, compression, bank pitch, sensor spacing and receiver geometry are our untested hypotheses. No team CAD, 1690 images or videos were inspected for this concept. The local 2056 report covers selected PDF pages, not the complete packages; no native CAD was measured. No reference establishes these dimensions, successful contact continuity, timing, motor sizing, deployment date, manufacture or legality.

Blank chassis is 700 x 760 mm, x=-350..350, y=0..760. Keep the full bumper ring intact, including side-section front band y=-85..0, z=45..165; any recess is internal chassis/bellypan only. Nominal coral is L301.625 x OD114.3 mm. For a horizontal coral at any yaw, use the deliberately conservative longitudinal half-envelope L/2+R=207.9625 mm. Therefore the entire crossing interval for its center is y=-292.9625..207.9625, not just y=-85..0. The piece-center polyline stays at z>=236.69 throughout that interval, exceeding the required 165+57.15+10=232.15 mm; the drawn minimum bottom-to-bumper margin is 14.54 mm. This is an arithmetic 2D horizontal-envelope hypothesis, not measured clearance; pitched/vertical entries, flex and complete swept volumes remain unverified. Acquisition: powered lower packets lift toward the OD74 kicker under an individually floating OD64 top row. Supported flat PC fingers bridge packet gaps; retain the OD74 rear powered row at y=-222, 78 mm behind the kicker, with 4 mm between their drawn envelopes. Approximate 15 mm top float, 6 mm plate thickness, packet dimensions and shaft datum strips are placeholders; thin plan strips locate shafts and do not claim continuous wheel-diameter cylinders. Side ramp and roller projections can overlap only as interleaved guide fingers at different x; shaft/rib holes and actual fits remain unsolved. Plan transverse rows match side y, with lower/kicker/rear axes at z45/151/151 and floating top at z285. Bank wheels have vertical axes and proposed z205..285 contact envelopes, above the rear-wheel top z188 where plan footprints overlap. Orientation: L and R each power all seven wheels on their own bank; first pair x=+/-171,y=-175 overlaps the rear acquisition contact region, then 90 mm station spacing converges to x=+/-80 and continues to y365 through cradle side windows y335..395. Capture crosswise/skewed coral, yaw toward +y and retain a nominal 110 mm lane against OD114.3; rotation sign, offsets, contact force and all intermediate yaw envelopes need tests. The centerline does not prove an orientation trajectory. A deliberate skew test must expose the symmetric crosswise jam case. Current-detected brief opposed bank commands are a reference-inspired recovery proposal, not a tested threshold, speed or retry policy. Cradle: supported entry rises 5 mm then drops behind an anti-bounce step, with open top and side access y460..540 for a gripper. D1 at y540 first slows/stops the piece; a controlled creep proposal resumes only if the receiver is ready and D1 remains valid. For nominal along-y coral, D1 is reached near center y389.19 while its tail is near y238.38, still between powered stations. D2 at y644 is reached near center y493.19 and requests, rather than blindly executes, handoff. The final bank pair at y365 retains drive through both events and the stop: at final center y500, the trailing end is y349.1875, still 15.8125 mm forward of that station. No unpowered coast or early gripper traction is assumed. Stop the banks and retain one coral in the supported stopped cradle while the gripper approaches, confirms capture and takes ownership. The stop at y650.8125 is simply receiver center y500 plus nominal L/2, not a measured team dimension or a tolerance. Final target is x0,y500,z245.15 with yaw0, one coral only. Require receiver-ready, pose/capture confirmation and valid D1/D2 ordering before release; blocked/missing beams, timeout, overrun or failed capture stop motion and require bounded retry or driver abort. Beam count is two events, not four endpoint channels. Whole-robot occupancy inhibits a second coral from acquisition until confirmed release. Flat router-cut aluminum/PC plates, located tabs, turned spacers and machined support blocks replace accurate bends; printed guides remain replaceable nonqualified parts. The plan movingOutline is only an acquisition-module envelope; it is not a whole-nose floating four-bar, a swept volume or a verified stow. states: Stage 2 only; all geometry, pickup, centering, grip and physical performance are UNTESTED. This option alone expressly overrides BRIEF.md's intact-bumper constraint: remove the real front bumper at x=-175..175, y=-85..0, through its full nominal z=45..165 section, retaining the flanking bumpers. The removed nominal segment is dashed reference only, never a working bumper or over-bumper path. Separately recess the central chassis at x=-175..175, y=0..340; there is no front frame member crossing the coral. The rear frame begins at y=340. This is a known 2025 R401/R402/R405 conflict, confirmed by Q152, not unknown legality and not an internal recess mislabeled as a bumper gap. It is ineligible as a 2025 competition recommendation. The first cheap test is the rules gate, which this geometry fails; no powered competition prototype is justified. Remaining paper checks and any future separately authorized non-competition bench tests cannot cure that rule conflict. Coordinates are approximate mm. Nominal coral is 301.625 mm long and 114.3 mm OD, offered crosswise at x=0, y=240, z=95. The 500 mm usable mouth narrows to 330 mm between guides within the separate 350 mm bumper opening. A centered crosswise coral has 24.1875 mm nominal clearance per bumper end, reduced to 14.1875 mm per inner guide; these are static dimensions, not demonstrated capture tolerance. Pickup: drive forward to bring coral onto the shallow tray and into the rearward-running lower surface of one compliant upper belt. Two 50 mm diameter transverse drums drive a 220 mm wide belt; one motor, no lift linkage, powered yaw stage or roller ladder. Passive guides propose centering a near-crosswise entry; arbitrary-yaw capture is not established. The tray top rises from floor at y=-420 to 37.85 mm at the receiver and 42.4379 mm at y=320. The path follows that support plus the nominal 57.15 mm radius, with shallow-slope tangency rounded by less than 0.1 mm; it passes through the missing bumper band at about z=76..81, never over the nominal bumper. Flat router-cut side plates support a straight inclined tray with a tapered printed entry lip; no precision bends. The belt's roughly 2 mm nominal interference is only a compliance hypothesis, not proven traction or preload. Hold: stop the belt with one coral supported on the tray; backdrive, braking and rollback remain unknown. Offer: confirm receiver-ready, close the two end jaws, confirm capture, then release the feed. Whole-robot occupancy must inhibit a second coral; sensing is not implemented. At the receiver the central 220 mm belt and narrowed tray leave 40.8125 mm of each coral end exposed. Open jaw faces at x=+/-156 have 5.1875 mm nominal end clearance; approach from above the exposed ends, then close inward. No crossbar or placeholder frame occupies the piece. The receiver's circular side envelope spans y=182.85..297.15, inside the 340 mm recess with 42.85 mm nominal rear clearance. Jaw fingers, their supporting structure, drive mounts and all loads require later design. This fixed deployed sketch has no demonstrated stow, floor compliance, jam reversal, finite-piece sweep or safe retention; physical unknowns remain separate from the already-known bumper rule violation.

title: Bore-Lock Elevator

summary: End-on robot approach seats a compliant bore mandrel. Internal pads hold during vertical lift; an outside saddle accepts coral before mandrel withdrawal and receiver retraction.
advantage: Straight router-cut plates, linear slides, turned drawbar and compliant pads need no accurate bends. The 350 mm approach span is not the narrow bore-alignment window.
risk: Dirty-bore grip and forced release are unproved. Horizontal lift is assumed; pitch, flex and stow need tests. The whole tube must clear the bumper before inward transfer.

states: Seat -> expand/hold -> lift -> outside latch -> captive-cam collapse/strip/withdraw -> park high -> receiver inward. One coral total; occupancy lockout. Pitch/stow open.

Solid contacts show raised offer; ghosts show capture at [-280,95]. A proposed 90-deg carrier turn follows the sampled arc; deployment linkage is unresolved, not a measured pivot.
